description: Thieves used copied keys to swap gold bullion for lead shot aboard a cross-Channel mail train running between London and Paris.

name: irish-crown-jewels-theft
description: The jeweled insignia of the Order of St Patrick vanished from a locked strongroom in Dublin Castle and was never recovered.

name: mona-lisa-theft
description: A Louvre employee hid inside the museum overnight and walked out the next morning with Leonardo da Vinci's painting under his coat.

name: ponzi-scheme-exposed
description: Charles Ponzi's investment scheme promising huge returns on postal reply coupons collapsed, exposed as paying old investors with new money.

name: kreuger-empire-collapse
description: Swedish financier Ivar Kreuger, known as the Match King, died as investigators found his global empire built on forged bonds.

name: just-judges-panel-theft
friendly_name: Theft of the Just Judges Panel
description: A panel of the Ghent Altarpiece was stolen from a Belgian cathedral overnight and, despite a ransom note, has never been found.

name: amber-room-looted
description: Occupying forces dismantled the ornate Amber Room from a Russian imperial palace near Leningrad and shipped it away for good.

name: van-meegeren-fake-vermeer-sale
description: Dutch forger Han van Meegeren sold a fabricated Vermeer painting through an intermediary to a senior Nazi official for a vast sum.

name: great-train-robbery-buckinghamshire
description: A gang ambushed a Royal Mail train in Buckinghamshire and made off with more than two and a half million pounds in banknotes.

name: caravaggio-nativity-theft
description: Caravaggio's altarpiece was cut from its frame and stolen from an oratory in Palermo, reportedly taken to order by the Sicilian Mafia.

name: baker-street-robbery
description: Burglars tunneled from a rented leather shop into the vault of a London bank and emptied dozens of safe deposit boxes overnight.

name: russborough-house-art-heist
description: An armed raid on an Irish country house saw the owners tied up while nineteen paintings, including a Vermeer, were cut from their frames.

name: lufthansa-heist
description: A crew of robbers raided a Lufthansa cargo terminal at JFK Airport and stole millions in cash and jewelry, still largely unsolved.

name: brinks-mat-robbery
description: Robbers who broke into a warehouse near Heathrow Airport expecting cash instead found and stole roughly three tonnes of gold bullion.

name: gardner-museum-art-heist
description: Two men disguised as police officers talked their way into a Boston museum overnight and stole thirteen artworks that remain missing.

name: theft-of-the-scream
description: Burglars used a ladder to break into an Oslo gallery and steal Edvard Munch's painting on the opening day of the Winter Olympics.

name: van-gogh-museum-theft
description: Two thieves climbed to the roof of Amsterdam's Van Gogh Museum and stole two paintings, later recovered from an Italian crime clan.

name: antwerp-diamond-heist
description: A gang cracked a supposedly impregnable vault beneath Antwerp's diamond district and emptied it of gems, gold and cash.

name: northern-bank-robbery
description: Armed robbers held bank employees' families hostage overnight to force staff to hand over a record cash haul from a Belfast vault.

name: madoff-ponzi-scheme-unravels
description: Financier Bernie Madoff confessed to his sons that his investment advisory business was a Ponzi scheme worth an estimated fifty billion dollars.

name: paris-modern-art-museum-heist
description: A lone thief cut through a padlocked gate and a window at a Paris museum and stole five paintings, including works by Picasso and Matisse.

name: kunsthal-rotterdam-art-heist
description: Thieves broke into a Dutch gallery overnight and stole seven paintings by artists including Picasso, Monet and Matisse in minutes.

name: hatton-garden-vault-burglary
description: A crew of elderly burglars drilled through a wall into a London safe deposit vault over a holiday weekend and cleared out dozens of boxes.

name: bangladesh-bank-cyber-heist
description: Hackers used fraudulent messages on a global banking network to try to steal nearly a billion dollars from a central bank's reserves.

name: dresden-green-vault-heist
description: Thieves broke into a Dresden museum's historic jewel collection overnight and stole eighteenth century treasures worth tens of millions of euros.

name: thespis-first-actor
description: A performer named Thespis reportedly stepped from the chorus to speak lines alone at a festival in Athens, later credited as the first actor.

name: oresteia-trilogy-premieres
description: Aeschylus's trilogy the Oresteia won first prize at a dramatic festival in Athens, the only complete Greek tragic trilogy to survive.

name: lysistrata-premieres
description: Aristophanes's comedy about women withholding intimacy to end a war was staged in Athens, establishing satirical stage comedy as a form.

name: theatre-of-epidaurus-built
description: A stone theatre built at Epidaurus in Greece became famed for its acoustics and still hosts performances, a model for later playhouses.

name: theatre-of-pompey-opens
description: A Roman general dedicated Rome's first permanent stone theatre, a vast complex able to seat tens of thousands of spectators.

name: san-cassiano-opera-house
description: Teatro San Cassiano opened in Venice as the first opera house built for a paying public, turning opera into a commercial art.

name: beggars-opera-premieres
description: A London stage show set satirical lyrics to popular tunes instead of composed arias, founding the ballad opera as a new form.

name: la-scala-opens
description: Teatro alla Scala opened in Milan and grew into one of the world's most influential opera houses.

name: magic-flute-premieres
description: Mozart's singspiel about a prince's magical trial by fire and water premiered in Vienna, blending fairy tale and Masonic symbolism.

name: barber-of-seville-premieres
description: Rossini's comic opera about a resourceful barber premiered in Rome to a famously disastrous reception before becoming a beloved favorite.

name: la-sylphide-premieres
description: A ballet about a doomed love between a man and an ethereal spirit opened in Paris, popularizing dancing en pointe and launching Romantic ballet.

name: giselle-premieres
description: A ballet about a peasant girl who dies of heartbreak and returns as a spirit opened at the Paris Opera, becoming a Romantic ballet cornerstone.

name: la-traviata-premieres
description: Verdi's opera about a courtesan's doomed love premiered in Venice, an initial flop that grew into one of the most performed operas ever staged.

name: dolls-house-premieres
description: Ibsen's play about a wife who walks out on her marriage and children premiered in Copenhagen, launching modern realist stage drama.

name: earnest-premieres-london
description: Oscar Wilde's comedy of mistaken identities and double lives opened in London to great acclaim just before his public disgrace began.

name: stanislavski-seagull-triumph
description: A Moscow production of Chekhov's play succeeded where an earlier staging had flopped, establishing a naturalistic method of stage acting.

name: show-boat-premieres
description: A Broadway show about performers on a Mississippi riverboat fused songs with a serious plot, reshaping the American stage musical.

name: oklahoma-premieres
description: A Broadway musical set on the American frontier fully integrated song, dance and story, defining the modern book musical.

name: hair-opens-broadway
description: A rock musical celebrating countercultural youth and protest against war transferred to Broadway, bringing rock music to the stage musical.

name: chorus-line-premieres
description: A Broadway musical built from real dancers auditioning for a chorus line told their own stories, later winning the Pulitzer Prize.

name: cats-opens-west-end
friendly_name: Cats Opens in the West End
description: A musical built from poems about a tribe of cats opened in London, becoming one of the longest running musicals in stage history.

name: phantom-of-opera-premieres
description: A musical about a disfigured composer haunting a Paris opera house opened in London's West End and became a global stage phenomenon.

name: wicked-premieres-broadway
description: A Broadway musical retold the story of Oz from the perspective of its witches, becoming one of the stage's biggest modern hits.

name: hamilton-opens-broadway
description: A hip hop musical about an American founding father transferred to Broadway after an earlier off-Broadway run, becoming a cultural phenomenon.

name: peace-of-callias
description: Athens and Persia reportedly agreed terms closing decades of fighting, though scholars still dispute whether the treaty existed.

name: peace-of-nicias
description: Athens and Sparta signed a fifty year truce meant to close the first stage of their long war, though fighting later resumed.

name: peace-of-constance
description: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa recognized the self government of the Lombard League's cities, closing their long revolt.

name: peace-of-lodi
description: Milan, Venice and Naples ended their long fighting over Lombardy, opening decades of relative peace among Italian states.

name: treaty-of-picquigny
description: The kings of England and France agreed a truce that finally closed out their long running conflict over the French crown.

name: second-treaty-of-paris
description: Following the defeat at Waterloo, the allied powers imposed final peace terms on France, closing a long era of continental war.

name: treaty-of-guadalupe-hidalgo
description: Mexico ceded vast northern territories to the United States, closing a war fought over the disputed Texas border.

name: treaty-of-paris-crimean-war
description: Russia and the allied powers signed terms closing their war over the Black Sea, which the treaty declared neutral waters.

name: peace-of-prague
description: Austria and Prussia signed terms closing their brief war, with Prussia absorbing several German states into its orbit.

name: geneva-accords-indochina
description: France and the Viet Minh signed terms closing their colonial war, splitting Vietnam into a northern and southern zone.

name: sneferu-red-pyramid
description: Pharaoh Sneferu completed the Red Pyramid at Dahshur, the first successful smooth sided true pyramid ever raised.

name: menkaure-pyramid-giza
description: Pharaoh Menkaure completed the third and smallest pyramid at Giza, finishing the trio beside Khufu and Khafre's monuments.

name: mentuhotep-ii-reunification
description: Pharaoh Mentuhotep II defeated rival dynasties and reunited Upper and Lower Egypt, ending a fractured intermediate period.

name: amenemhat-i-founds-dynasty
description: A former vizier named Amenemhat I seized the Egyptian throne and founded a new dynasty, moving the capital southward.

name: hatshepsut-becomes-pharaoh
description: Hatshepsut assumed full pharaonic titles and regalia, ruling as king rather than merely as regent for her stepson.

name: seti-i-recovers-levant
description: Pharaoh Seti I took the Egyptian throne and campaigned into the Levant, recovering territory lost during religious upheaval.

name: abu-simbel-temples-dedicated
description: Pharaoh Ramesses II dedicated his rock cut temples at Abu Simbel, fronted by four colossal seated statues of himself.

name: merneptah-victory-stele
description: Pharaoh Merneptah repelled a Libyan invasion and commemorated the victory on a stele naming a people called Israel.

name: ramesses-iii-sea-peoples
description: Pharaoh Ramesses III defeated a coalition of seaborne raiders known as the Sea Peoples in major land and naval battles.

name: ramesses-iii-assassinated
description: A palace conspiracy led by a secondary wife of Pharaoh Ramesses III ended his life, confirmed later by forensic study.

name: piye-conquers-egypt
description: The Nubian king Piye marched north, defeated a coalition of Delta rulers, and became pharaoh over a reunited Egypt.

name: taharqa-crowned-pharaoh
description: Taharqa became pharaoh of the Nubian dynasty ruling Egypt, presiding over an empire stretching into the Levant.

name: psamtik-i-reunifies-egypt
description: Pharaoh Psamtik I expelled Assyrian backed rivals from the Nile Delta and reunited Egypt under native rule once more.

name: necho-ii-defeats-josiah
description: Pharaoh Necho II's army killed King Josiah of Judah in battle while marching north to reinforce a crumbling Assyrian ally.

name: cambyses-conquers-egypt
description: Persian king Cambyses II defeated the Egyptian pharaoh at Pelusium, ending native rule and folding Egypt into his empire.

name: nectanebo-i-founds-dynasty
description: Nectanebo I seized the Egyptian throne, founded the country's last native dynasty, and repelled an invading Persian army.

name: last-native-pharaoh-flees
description: Pharaoh Nectanebo II, defeated by a renewed Persian invasion, abandoned Egypt and ended native pharaonic rule for good.

name: alexander-crowned-pharaoh
description: Alexander the Great entered Egypt without resistance and was crowned pharaoh at Memphis by the local priesthood.

name: rome-war-on-queen-teuta
friendly_name: Rome Makes War on Queen Teuta
description: Rome sent a fleet and army against Illyrian queen Teuta after her state sponsored raiders preyed on Adriatic shipping, forcing her surrender.

name: caesar-captured-cilician-pirates
description: Julius Caesar was seized by Cilician pirates in the Aegean, held for ransom for weeks, and later hunted down and executed his captors as promised.

name: pompey-sweeps-mediterranean-pirates
description: Given sweeping emergency powers, Pompey cleared the Mediterranean of the pirate fleets that had strangled Rome's grain supply in a single season.

name: vikings-sack-paris
description: A Norse fleet under Ragnar sailed up the Seine and besieged Paris, extracting a huge ransom of silver from the Frankish king for withdrawing.

name: stortebeker-executed-hamburg
description: Baltic pirate captain Klaus Stortebeker, leader of the Victual Brothers, was captured at sea by Hamburg's fleet and beheaded with dozens of his crew.

name: barbarossa-brothers-seize-algiers
description: Corsair brothers Aruj and Hayreddin Barbarossa seized control of Algiers, turning it into the base of Ottoman aligned piracy in the western sea.

name: battle-of-preveza
description: Corsair admiral Barbarossa's Ottoman fleet routed a Holy League armada off western Greece, securing corsair dominance of the sea for decades.

name: wokou-raiders-besiege-nanjing
description: At the peak of the wokou crisis, Japanese led pirate bands raided deep into China and briefly besieged the great walled city of Nanjing.

name: qi-jiguang-crushes-wokou
description: Ming general Qi Jiguang's newly trained militia routed wokou pirate bands in a string of battles, breaking the raiders' hold on the Zhejiang coast.

name: drake-raids-nombre-de-dios
description: English privateer Francis Drake attacked the Spanish treasure port of Nombre de Dios in Panama, opening his campaign against Spain's silver route.

name: drake-knighted-golden-hind
description: Queen Elizabeth I knighted Francis Drake aboard the Golden Hind, publicly rewarding a career of privateering raids against Spanish shipping.

name: grace-omalley-meets-elizabeth
description: Irish pirate chieftain Grace O'Malley sailed to London and negotiated directly with Elizabeth I over her clan's maritime raiding and captured sons.

name: piet-heyn-captures-treasure-fleet
description: Dutch privateer admiral Piet Heyn captured an entire Spanish silver fleet intact off Cuba, the richest prize ever taken from Spain at sea.

name: corsairs-sack-baltimore-ireland
description: Barbary corsairs raided the Irish village of Baltimore, capturing most of its inhabitants to sell into slavery in North Africa.

name: morgan-sacks-panama-city
description: Buccaneer Henry Morgan led a force across the isthmus and burned Panama City, one of the largest raids of the whole buccaneering era.

name: every-raids-ganj-i-sawai
description: Pirate Henry Every captured the Mughal treasure ship Ganj-i-Sawai in the Indian Ocean, the richest single pirate haul on record.

name: captain-kidd-hanged-london
description: William Kidd, commissioned as a privateer but tried as a pirate, was hanged at Execution Dock after a trial that became a public sensation.

name: blackbeard-killed-ocracoke
description: Royal Navy lieutenant Robert Maynard cornered and killed the pirate Blackbeard off the Carolina coast after a fierce shipboard fight.

name: bonny-read-convicted-piracy
friendly_name: Anne Bonny and Mary Read Convicted
description: The two women pirates, captured aboard Calico Jack Rackham's sloop off Jamaica, were tried and convicted of piracy but escaped hanging.

name: bartholomew-roberts-killed
description: Black Bart Roberts, the most successful pirate of his age with hundreds of ships taken, was killed by cannon fire off West Africa in a naval battle.

name: vijaydurg-falls-to-british
description: A combined British and Maratha fleet stormed Tulaji Angre's fortress at Vijaydurg, ending the Angre family's decades of raiding on India's coast.

name: rachel-wall-hanged-piracy
description: American pirate Rachel Wall, who lured ships with fake distress signals off the New England coast, was hanged in Boston for robbery at sea.

name: surcouf-captures-kent
description: French corsair Robert Surcouf boarded and captured the much larger British merchant ship Kent in the Bay of Bengal with a small, outgunned crew.

name: decatur-burns-philadelphia
description: Stephen Decatur led a raid into Tripoli harbor to burn the captured USS Philadelphia, denying Barbary corsairs its use during the war against them.

name: zheng-yi-sao-fleet-surrenders
description: Pirate queen Zheng Yi Sao negotiated a mass amnesty for her tens of thousands of followers, ending the largest pirate confederation in history.

name: bombardment-algiers-slaves-freed
description: A British and Dutch fleet bombarded Algiers to force the release of Christian slaves and end Barbary corsair attacks on European shipping.

name: france-conquers-algiers
description: A French invasion force captured Algiers, toppling the Ottoman backed regency and ending three centuries of Barbary corsair power in North Africa.

name: spain-storms-balanguingui
description: A Spanish naval expedition stormed the fortified island of Balanguingui in the Sulu Sea, destroying a stronghold used by raiders to prey on shipping.

name: recaap-piracy-pact-signed
description: Sixteen Asian nations concluded the ReCAAP agreement in Tokyo, the first government to government treaty for sharing intelligence against piracy.

name: eu-operation-atalanta-launched
description: The European Union deployed its first joint naval mission to protect merchant shipping from Somali pirates off the Horn of Africa.

name: maersk-alabama-hijacked
description: Somali pirates hijacked the American flagged container ship Maersk Alabama, and Navy SEAL snipers later killed three pirates to free the captain.

name: somali-hijackings-fall-to-zero
description: For the first time since the surge began, a full year passed with no successful pirate hijacking of a large merchant vessel off the Somali coast.

name: gauls-sack-rome
description: Gallic warriors under Brennus routed Roman defenders and occupied much of the city before withdrawing with a ransom in gold.

name: pyrrhus-invades-italy
description: King Pyrrhus of Epirus landed an army with war elephants in southern Italy to defend Tarentum against Roman expansion.

name: justinian-becomes-emperor
description: Justinian I ascended the Byzantine throne and launched sweeping legal reform alongside campaigns to reclaim lost Roman territory.

name: ashurbanipal-library-founded
description: Assyrian king Ashurbanipal assembled a vast collection of cuneiform tablets at Nineveh, the earliest known systematically organized library.

name: alexandria-library-caesar-fire
description: Fires set during Julius Caesar's siege of Alexandria spread into the harbor district and damaged the great library's collection of scrolls.

name: nalanda-destroyed
description: A Turkic general's forces sacked and burned the Buddhist university at Nalanda, ending its long run as a center of learning.

name: house-of-wisdom-destroyed
description: Mongol forces sacked Baghdad and destroyed its great library, throwing so many books into the river that witnesses said the water turned black.

name: charles-university-prague
description: Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV founded a university at Prague, the oldest degree granting institution in Central Europe.

name: eton-college-founded
description: King Henry VI founded a school near Windsor meant to educate a set number of poor scholars free of charge.

name: leiden-university-founded
description: William of Orange founded a university at Leiden as a reward for the city's endurance through a long Spanish siege.

name: edinburgh-university-founded
description: Edinburgh's town council established a university under royal charter, the first in Britain founded by a municipal government.

name: harvard-college-founded
description: The Massachusetts Bay colony founded a college that became the first institution of higher learning in what is now the United States.

name: yale-founded
description: A group of Congregationalist ministers chartered a Collegiate School in Connecticut, later renamed for a generous benefactor.

name: princeton-founded
description: Evangelical Presbyterians chartered the College of New Jersey, which grew over time into Princeton University.

name: west-point-founded
description: Congress established a military academy on the Hudson River to train officers for the United States Army.

name: university-berlin-founded
description: Wilhelm von Humboldt founded a university in Berlin built around a new ideal linking scholarly research with teaching.

name: vassar-college-founded
description: Brewer Matthew Vassar chartered a college in New York dedicated to educating women to the same standard as men.

name: cornell-university-founded
description: Ezra Cornell and Andrew Dickson White founded a university in Ithaca open to any student regardless of background.

name: johns-hopkins-founded
description: A bequest from a Baltimore merchant founded a university modeled on German research institutions, reshaping American higher education.

name: stanford-university-founded
description: A railroad magnate and his wife founded a university in California in memory of their son, who died young.

name: louvain-library-burns
description: German troops burned the library of a Belgian university, destroying hundreds of thousands of volumes and rare manuscripts.

name: sarajevo-library-destroyed
description: Shelling during the siege of a Bosnian capital set fire to its national library, destroying most of its collection of books.

name: mosul-libraries-destroyed
description: Fighters occupying an Iraqi city burned its libraries, including a university's collection, as part of a wider campaign of destruction.

name: khufu-ship
description: Egyptian shipwrights buried a huge cedar vessel beside the Great Pyramid, its planks fitted together with mortise and tenon joints rather than nails.

name: phoenician-bireme
description: Phoenician shipwrights stacked a second bank of oars above the first, creating the bireme and roughly doubling a galley's rowing power.

name: greek-trireme
description: Greek and Phoenician navies built the trireme, a fast three tiered oared warship whose bronze ram dominated Mediterranean sea power for centuries.

name: lateen-sail-spreads
description: Mediterranean sailors adopted the triangular lateen sail, letting ships point much closer into the wind than a square rig ever could.

name: junk-watertight-bulkheads
description: Chinese junk builders divided their hulls into sealed compartments with internal bulkheads, so a single breach no longer sank the ship.

name: venice-founds-arsenal
description: The Republic of Venice opened its Arsenal shipyard, where standardized war galleys were assembled from pre made parts on a production line.

name: hanseatic-cog
description: The flat bottomed, single masted cog, fitted with a stern rudder and high sides, became the workhorse cargo ship of North Sea trade.

name: carrack-emerges
description: Mediterranean and Atlantic shipwrights combined a high sided hull with several masts of square and lateen sail, producing the carrack.

name: dutch-fluyt
description: Dutch builders launched the fluyt, a cheap, bulky cargo hull needing only a small crew, giving the Dutch Republic an edge in bulk trade.

name: hms-sovereign-of-the-seas
description: The Royal Navy launched Sovereign of the Seas, the first three decked warship carrying over a hundred guns, setting a pattern for centuries.

name: rattler-beats-alecto
description: The Royal Navy tied screw driven HMS Rattler stern to stern with paddle steamer Alecto, and Rattler towed her rival backward with ease.

name: flying-cloud-record-run
description: The clipper Flying Cloud sailed from New York to San Francisco around Cape Horn in under ninety days, a speed record that stood for a century.

name: french-ironclad-gloire
description: France launched Gloire, an iron armored wooden warship that instantly made every unarmored wooden battle fleet in the world obsolete.

name: hms-warrior-launches
description: Britain answered Gloire with Warrior, the first warship built entirely of iron rather than iron clad wood, starting a naval arms race.

name: cutty-sark-launches
description: The tea clipper Cutty Sark launched on the Clyde, one of the fastest sailing ships ever built just as steam was making clippers obsolete.

name: hms-havock-first-destroyer
description: The Royal Navy commissioned Havock, a fast torpedo boat destroyer built to hunt down the small boats that threatened its capital ships.

name: turbinia-storms-spithead
description: Charles Parsons raced his steam turbine yacht uninvited through a Royal Navy fleet review, outrunning every escort sent to stop him.

name: uss-holland-commissioned
description: The US Navy commissioned Holland, its first submarine, pairing an electric motor for running underwater with a gasoline engine on the surface.

name: hms-dreadnought-launches
description: Britain launched Dreadnought, an all big gun, turbine powered battleship so advanced it made every earlier battleship obsolete overnight.

name: bells-hydrofoil-record
description: Alexander Graham Bell's hydrofoil boat set a world water speed record on a Nova Scotia lake, riding on foils that lifted it above the waves.

name: ss-ideal-x-sails
description: The converted tanker Ideal X carried dozens of truck trailers from Newark to Houston on the first commercial voyage of a container ship.

name: ns-lenin-enters-service
description: The Soviet Union commissioned Lenin, the first nuclear powered surface ship, an icebreaker built to keep Arctic shipping lanes open year round.

name: caspian-sea-monster-flies
description: A huge Soviet craft made its first flight skimming just above the water on a cushion of trapped air, neither floating nor truly flying.

name: yara-birkeland-launches
description: Norway launched Yara Birkeland, the first fully electric, autonomous container ship, designed to sail without fuel or a crew aboard.

name: assyrian-siege-lachish
description: Assyrian forces under Sennacherib stormed the fortified Judean city, an assault later carved in detail on palace relief panels.

name: fall-of-babylon-cyrus
description: Persian forces under Cyrus the Great took the heavily fortified capital, reportedly diverting a river to slip beneath its walls.

name: athenian-siege-syracuse
description: Athenian forces blockaded the Sicilian city for two years during a war with Sparta, ending in disastrous defeat for the invaders.

name: alexanders-siege-tyre
description: Alexander the Great besieged the island stronghold for seven months, building a stone causeway to bring his army to its walls.

name: viking-siege-of-paris
description: A massive Viking fleet blockaded the fortified island city on the Seine for months, unable to break through its defenses.

name: third-crusade-siege-acre
description: Crusader forces besieged the fortified port for two years before its garrison finally surrendered during the Third Crusade.

name: siege-of-orleans
description: English forces besieged the city until Joan of Arc's relief army broke through, turning the fortunes of a long war in France.

name: ottoman-siege-rhodes
description: Ottoman forces besieged the Knights Hospitaller until the defenders surrendered the island's heavily fortified capital.

name: great-siege-of-malta
description: A massive Ottoman fleet besieged the Knights Hospitaller on the island for months before withdrawing in costly defeat.

name: siege-of-sevastopol
description: Allied forces besieged the fortified Russian naval base for nearly a year, marked by grinding trench warfare and heavy losses.

name: siege-of-vicksburg
description: Union forces besieged the fortified river city for weeks, forcing its surrender and giving the North control of the river.

name: prussian-siege-of-paris
description: Prussian forces encircled and bombarded the French capital for months, starving its residents into surrender during a war with Germany.

name: siege-of-khartoum
description: Mahdist forces besieged the Sudanese capital for months, storming its defenses and killing the British general just before help arrived.

name: siege-of-mafeking
description: Boer forces besieged the small British garrison town for over two hundred days until a relief column finally broke through.

name: siege-of-bastogne
description: German forces surrounded American paratroopers holding a snowbound Belgian town, who famously refused a demand to surrender.

name: siege-of-dien-bien-phu
description: Viet Minh forces besieged a French fortress in the highlands for weeks, a defeat that ended French colonial rule in the region.

name: battle-to-retake-mosul
description: Iraqi and coalition forces surrounded an Islamic State stronghold and fought street by street for months to retake the city.

name: red-pyramid-sneferu
description: Pharaoh Sneferu completed a smooth sided pyramid at Dahshur, briefly the tallest structure on Earth before his son's tomb surpassed it.

name: lincoln-cathedral-spire
description: The central spire of Lincoln Cathedral in England was finished, ending the Great Pyramid's long reign as the tallest structure on Earth.

name: lincoln-spire-collapses
description: A storm toppled the central spire of Lincoln Cathedral, ending its long run as the tallest structure in the world.

name: st-olafs-tallinn-spire
description: The newly finished spire of St. Olaf's Church in Tallinn became the tallest structure anywhere in the world.

name: beauvais-cathedral-collapse
description: The unfinished central tower of Beauvais Cathedral in France, briefly the tallest spire in Europe, collapsed only years after completion.

name: st-olafs-spire-burns
description: A lightning strike set fire to St. Olaf's Church in Tallinn, destroying the spire that had made it the world's tallest structure.

name: strasbourg-cathedral-tallest
description: With St. Olaf's spire gone, Strasbourg Cathedral was recognized as the tallest structure on Earth, a title it kept for two centuries.

name: st-nicholas-church-hamburg
description: A soaring new spire completed on St. Nicholas Church in Hamburg made it the tallest building anywhere in the world.

name: rouen-cathedral-iron-spire
description: A new cast iron spire completed atop Rouen Cathedral in France briefly made it the tallest building in the world.

name: cologne-cathedral-completed
description: After more than six centuries of work, Cologne Cathedral was finished and became the tallest building on Earth, the last church to hold the title.

name: washington-monument-completed
description: The obelisk honoring George Washington was completed in the capital, becoming the tallest structure on Earth and the first secular one to hold it.

name: woolworth-building-opens
description: Frank Woolworth's ornate Gothic tower opened in New York and became the tallest building on Earth, a title it held for the next seventeen years.

name: bank-of-manhattan-trust-tops-out
description: The Bank of Manhattan Trust tower at 40 Wall Street topped out in New York, briefly becoming the tallest building in the world.

name: kvly-tv-mast-erected
description: A guyed television transmission mast rose in rural North Dakota, becoming the tallest human made structure anywhere on Earth.

name: ostankino-tower-completed
description: The Ostankino Tower opened in Moscow, becoming the tallest freestanding structure that had ever been built.

name: world-trade-center-tops-out
description: The North Tower of New York's World Trade Center topped out, surpassing the Empire State Building as the tallest building on Earth.

name: warsaw-radio-mast-erected
description: A guyed radio mast near Konstantynow in Poland was completed, becoming the tallest human made structure ever built.

name: warsaw-mast-collapses
description: The record setting Warsaw radio mast collapsed during maintenance work, handing the title of tallest structure back to an American tower.

name: water-buffalo-domesticated
description: Farmers across South and East Asia tamed wild water buffalo for plowing fields and producing milk.

name: hierakonpolis-royal-menagerie
description: Elite burials in southern Egypt reveal captive elephants, hippos, baboons and wildcats kept as a show of status.

name: dromedary-camel-domesticated
description: Herders on the Arabian Peninsula domesticated the one humped camel for milk, meat and desert transport.

name: falconry-emerges-central-asia
description: Hunters on the Asian steppe began training captured raptors to hunt cooperatively alongside people.

name: kikkuli-horse-training-text
description: A Hittite trainer named Kikkuli set down a long conditioning program for chariot horses, the oldest known training text for any animal.

name: rome-sacred-geese-alarm
description: Geese kept on Rome's Capitoline Hill cried out and woke the garrison during a night assault on the city.

name: hydaspes-war-elephants
description: Alexander the Great overcame King Porus and his war elephant corps in a hard fought battle in India.

name: mutina-pigeon-messengers
friendly_name: Pigeons Break the Siege of Mutina
description: Trapped inside besieged Mutina, Decimus Brutus sent messages out by pigeon to reach his allied consuls.

name: general-stud-book-published
description: James Weatherby published a registry tracing every listed racehorse back to a handful of founding sires.

name: jardin-des-plantes-zoo-opens
description: Revolutionary France turned former royal animal collections into the Jardin des Plantes, an early public zoo.

name: barry-rescue-dog-legend
description: The St Bernard credited with saving dozens of Alpine travelers died peacefully in retirement in Bern.

name: london-zoo-opens-regents-park
description: The Zoological Society of London opened its gardens in Regent's Park to the paying public.

name: first-formal-dog-show
description: Newcastle upon Tyne hosted what is regarded as the first organized conformation show for dogs.

name: kennel-club-founded-britain
description: Britain formed the world's first kennel club to standardize dog breeds and keep a breed registry.

name: old-hemp-border-collie-ancestor
description: A working sheepdog born in Northumberland became the ancestor of nearly every modern Border Collie.

name: beersheba-cavalry-charge
description: Australian Light Horse troops made a mounted charge that broke Ottoman lines defending a town in Palestine.

name: seeing-eye-guide-dog-school
description: A New Jersey town became home to the first American school training dogs to guide blind handlers.

name: izbushensky-cavalry-charge
description: Italian cavalry made a mounted saber charge against Soviet lines, remembered as one of the last true cavalry charges.

name: przewalski-horses-rewilded
description: Captive bred Przewalski's horses were released onto the Mongolian steppe, restoring the last truly wild horse.

name: trepanation-earliest-known
description: Archaeologists found a skull with a hole deliberately cut into it that later healed, the oldest solid evidence of a patient surviving cranial surgery.

name: hippocratic-surgical-texts
description: Greek physicians circulated treatises on fractures and head wounds that set out systematic surgical technique, including reducing dislocated joints.

name: first-appendectomy
description: A London surgeon removed a boy's perforated appendix in the middle of a routine hernia operation, the earliest recorded case to succeed.

name: mcdowell-first-ovariotomy
description: A Kentucky surgeon removed a massive ovarian tumor from a fully conscious patient on her own kitchen table, the first such operation to succeed.

name: rehn-sutures-heart-wound
description: A Frankfurt surgeon closed a stab wound to a patient's heart with sutures, the first successful operation performed on the organ itself.

name: citrate-blood-storage
description: Physicians found that adding sodium citrate stopped donated blood from clotting, letting it be stored ahead of need rather than given directly.

name: magill-endotracheal-tube
description: Treating disfigured war veterans, a surgeon devised a flexible tube placed in the windpipe to keep patients breathing safely under anesthesia.

name: first-blue-baby-operation
description: Surgeons rerouted an infant's blood vessels to relieve a heart defect that was starving her body of oxygen, founding pediatric heart surgery.

name: heart-lung-machine-first-use
description: A surgeon used his own heart-lung machine to keep a patient alive while he repaired a hole in her heart, opening the era of open-heart surgery.

name: first-hand-transplant
description: Surgeons in Lyon grafted a donor hand onto a recipient's arm, the first hand transplant, though it was later removed at the patient's own request.

name: da-vinci-surgical-robot
description: Regulators cleared a robotic surgical system that lets a surgeon operate through mechanical arms guided from a console across the room.

name: hammurabi-surgeon-laws
description: Babylon's law code set a surgeon's fee for a successful operation and ordered his hand cut off if a noble patient died under the bronze lancet.

name: walls-of-uruk-raised
description: Sumerian Uruk was ringed with a great defensive wall, later credited in legend to King Gilgamesh.

name: walls-of-babylon-rebuilt
description: A Babylonian king rebuilt and strengthened the city's massive double walls, later ranked among the ancient wonders.

name: long-walls-of-athens-built
description: Athens built parallel fortified walls linking the city to its port, securing supply lines against any siege.

name: long-walls-of-athens-torn-down
description: After its defeat in a long war with Sparta, Athens was forced to tear down the Long Walls as a peace condition.

name: servian-wall-of-rome-built
description: Rome raised a defensive stone wall around the city following a Gallic sack, enclosing its seven hills.

name: herod-builds-masada-fortress
description: A Judean king built a lavish mountaintop fortress and palace complex overlooking the Dead Sea.

name: antonine-wall-built
description: Rome pushed its British frontier north and built a turf wall across the narrow waist of Scotland.

name: aurelian-walls-encircle-rome
description: An emperor built a massive brick wall circuit around Rome itself in response to barbarian incursions.

name: theodosian-walls-completed
description: Constantinople's triple land walls were finished, making the city nearly impregnable for many centuries.

name: sigiriya-rock-fortress-raised
description: A king built a palace fortress atop a sheer granite rock in Sri Lanka as a defensible new capital.

name: walls-of-benin-city-built
description: Over generations the Edo people raised an enormous system of earthen walls and moats around Benin City.

name: krak-des-chevaliers-rebuilt
description: A crusading military order rebuilt this Syrian castle into one of the most formidable fortresses of its era.

name: malbork-castle-built
description: A crusading military order raised what became the largest brick castle in the world beside a northern river.

name: carcassonne-refortified
description: The French crown had the double walled fortress city of Carcassonne reinforced against English raids.

name: kumbhalgarh-fort-built
description: A Rajasthani ruler built this hill fort, ringed by one of the longest continuous walls anywhere in the world.

name: suleiman-rebuilds-jerusalem-walls
description: An Ottoman sultan had the walls around Jerusalem's Old City torn down and reconstructed during his long reign.

name: cartagena-walls-begun
description: Spain began fortifying its Caribbean port of Cartagena with massive stone walls to guard against pirate raids.

name: fort-ticonderoga-built
description: France built this star shaped fort at a strategic chokepoint between two lakes in its northern colonies.

name: france-builds-maginot-line
description: France began constructing a chain of concrete fortifications along its German border to deter another invasion.

name: warsaw-ghetto-wall-built
description: German occupiers walled off a district of Warsaw to seal in the city's Jewish population.

name: germany-builds-atlantic-wall
description: Germany constructed thousands of bunkers and fortifications along the European coast to repel an Allied invasion.

name: korean-dmz-fortified
description: After an armistice, both Koreas fortified the buffer zone between them with fences, walls and guard posts.

name: israel-builds-west-bank-barrier
description: Israel began building a wall and fence system through and around the West Bank during a period of conflict.

name: us-secure-fence-act-signed
description: The US president signed a law authorizing hundreds of miles of new fencing along the border with Mexico.

name: lagash-girsu-canal-network
description: The Sumerian city of Lagash expanded a web of irrigation canals around Girsu, a network later disputed fiercely with neighboring Umma.

name: mohenjo-daro-covered-drains
description: Builders in the Indus city of Mohenjo-daro laid brick lined covered drains and wells, an early planned sewage and water system.

name: earliest-persian-qanats
description: Engineers on the Iranian plateau began tunneling gently sloped qanats, carrying groundwater to farms without pumps or evaporation.

name: great-dam-of-marib
description: Sabaean rulers in Yemen raised a great earthen dam across a desert valley, irrigating a vast oasis for many centuries.

name: sennacherib-jerwan-aqueduct
description: Assyrian king Sennacherib finished a stone aqueduct at Jerwan, among the oldest aqueducts known, to water Nineveh's gardens.

name: dujiangyan-irrigation-system
description: Engineer Li Bing built Dujiangyan on the Min River, splitting its flow without a dam to irrigate the Sichuan plain below.

name: petra-nabataean-water-system
description: The Nabataeans carved channels, cisterns and small dams into Petra's cliffs to capture flash floods for their desert city.

name: sigiriya-water-gardens
description: A Sri Lankan king's builders laid out gravity fed channels, pools and fountains at Sigiriya that still function to this day.

name: basilica-cistern-built
description: Byzantine builders raised a vast underground cistern in Constantinople to store aqueduct water for the imperial capital.

name: marib-dam-collapses
description: Yemen's aging Marib Dam burst after centuries of patched repairs, scattering local tribes and ending its oasis's irrigation.

name: hohokam-canal-network
description: The Hohokam people expanded a major canal network off a desert river, irrigating land in the Sonoran Desert near modern Phoenix.

name: machu-picchu-water-channels
description: Inca builders carved a network of stone channels and fountains carrying spring water through the mountaintop citadel.

name: chapultepec-aqueduct
description: Aztec engineers built a double aqueduct from Chapultepec's springs to carry fresh water across the lake to their capital.

name: beemster-polder-drained
description: Dutch investors drained a large lake using windmill pumps and a ring canal, creating the first large reclaimed polder.

name: great-level-fens-drained
description: An engineer finished draining a vast stretch of eastern English marshland into new channels, turning fen into farmland.

name: croton-aqueduct-opens
description: New York City opened a long masonry aqueduct carrying river water dozens of kilometers south into Manhattan.

name: chicago-river-reversal
description: A new sanitary and ship canal reversed a city river's flow, sending Chicago's sewage away from its drinking water source.

name: la-aqueduct-owens-valley
description: A civil engineer's aqueduct began carrying distant valley water hundreds of kilometers to fuel a growing desert city.

name: afsluitdijk-completed
description: The Netherlands completed a long dyke closing off a shallow sea inlet, turning it into a large freshwater lake.

name: thames-barrier-completed
description: London finished a row of rotating steel gates across its river that can seal the waterway against storm surges.
